title: Container with most water
prompt:
You are given an array heights where heights[i] is the height of a vertical wall at position i. Choose two walls. Together with the ground they hold water up to the shorter wall's height, across the distance between them: Math.min(heights[left], heights[right]) * (right - left).

Write maxWater(heights) that returns the largest amount of water any two walls can hold. With fewer than two walls, return 0. Aim for O(n) time; the all-pairs version is O(n²).

Example: maxWater([1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7]) → 49 (walls at index 1 and 8: min(8, 7) × 7).

Constraints: 0 ≤ heights.length ≤ 105, 0 ≤ heights[i] ≤ 104.

tests.name: best pair is the two ends
best pair is in the middle
fewer than two walls holds nothing
matches the all-pairs answer on many small inputs

hints: All pairs is O(n²). Start with the widest possible container: one pointer at each end. Every later container is narrower, so it only wins if its water level is higher.

Compare the two walls. The shorter one caps the water level for every container it is part of, and all other containers using it are narrower. So it can never beat what you just measured: move that pointer inward.

Shape:

let left = 0, right = heights.length - 1, best = 0;
while (left < right) {
  best = Math.max(best, Math.min(heights[left], heights[right]) * (right - left));
  if (heights[left] < heights[right]) left++;
  else right--;
}
return best;
explain:
Time O(n), space O(1). Each step discards one wall for good, so there are at most n − 1 steps. The all-pairs version does n(n − 1)/2 checks: about 5 billion for 100,000 walls.

The general lesson: two pointers work whenever you can prove that one end can't be part of a better answer. That proof is the whole solution; the code is five lines.

In an interview: "I'll start with the widest container and move inward. The shorter wall limits the water for every container it's in, and every other one is narrower, so I can discard it. That gives O(n) time and O(1) space instead of checking all pairs."
